source.title: Forgetting as a consequence of retrieval: a meta-analytic review of retrieval-induced forgetting

confidence_rationale: First major meta-analysis directly adjudicating the inhibition vs non-inhibition (strength competition / blocking) accounts of retrieval-induced forgetting. Results LARGELY support inhibition but also surface challenging evidence, with outcome depending on how RIF is measured. This is exactly the calibration Q-058 needs: it confirms inhibition is a distinct, real mechanism, while warning the distinction is not absolute. Marked 'mixed' to faithfully represent the meta-analytic verdict; high source quality (quantitative meta-analysis) gives reasonable confidence.
failure_signatures: The inhibition account is supported on average but not universally -- the result varies with how RIF is assessed (e.g. cue-independence tests), so a binary REE design decision ('always use an explicit inhibitory edge') would over-read the evidence.

Some findings are explicable by non-inhibitory mechanisms (strength-based competition/blocking), so REE cannot assume every observed competitive interaction requires a signed inhibitory coupling rather than local softmax.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A meta-analysis of the retrieval-induced-forgetting literature largely supports the view that an inhibitory mechanism reduces the accessibility of competing non-target items, but also finds challenging evidence consistent with non-inhibitory mechanisms (strength-based competition, blocking); the conclusion depends substantially on how retrieval-induced forgetting is operationalised and measured.
mapping.ree_translation: Calibrates Q-058: it confirms that an inhibitory mode is a genuine and distinct mechanism (so REE is right to consider explicit signed/inhibitory couplings beyond local softmax), while warning that the inhibition-vs-competition distinction is graded and measurement-dependent. Implies REE should treat 'needs an explicit sign' as a per-coupling empirical question (resolved by discriminating tests) rather than a blanket architectural rule.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Meta-analysis of human verbal/behavioural RIF studies; the inhibition is inferred behaviourally, and 'measurement-dependence' is about lab paradigms, not REE instrumentation. Transfer to REE inter-field couplings is a functional analogy; the meta-analysis says nothing about decommitment, residue-based veto, or waking/simulation/offline regimes specifically.
mapping.source_context: Quantitative meta-analysis, human retrieval-practice / RIF studies; compares inhibitory vs non-inhibitory theoretical accounts across many experiments.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality (first major meta-analysis, Psychological Bulletin). Mapping fidelity moderate -- behavioural, inferential, and about lab measurement choices; held as 'mixed' to honestly reflect the partial support.
